hook: The sultan who won back Jerusalem, admired by friend and foe for his mercy.

pages.x: Salah ad-Din Yusuf was born around 1137 in Tikrit, in Iraq, into a Kurdish family. His father and uncle served the Turkish ruler Nur ad-Din, and Saladin grew up in Damascus, at first more interested in religion than war.

In 1169 his uncle took him to Egypt, where he became chief minister to the Fatimid caliph. When the caliph died, he ended the dynasty, and after Nur ad-Din's death he united Egypt and Syria under his own rule.

In July 1187 he lured the Crusader army away from its water into hot, dry hills near the Sea of Galilee. Parched, and choked by smoke from fires his men set in the grass, the Crusaders were destroyed at the Horns of Hattin. The king of Jerusalem was taken prisoner.

Three months later Jerusalem surrendered. When the Crusaders took the city in 1099 they had slaughtered its people. Saladin let the Christians go for a ransom, and freed thousands of the poor who could not pay.

The Third Crusade brought Richard the Lionheart of England. They fought for a year but never met. When Richard's horse was killed at Jaffa, Saladin sent him two fresh horses; when Richard fell ill, he sent fruit and snow from the mountains. In 1192 they made peace.
Saladin gave away so much of his wealth that when he died in Damascus in 1193, there was not enough money in his treasury to pay for his funeral.
Saladin united much of the Muslim Middle East and won back Jerusalem. Muslims and Christians alike praised his mercy; Dante placed him among the noble souls in Limbo, beside Socrates and Plato.
pts: Founded the Ayyubid dynasty in Egypt and Syria
